And what Austin will do is write a book called City of God, putting the Catholic Church above Rome. He argues that Rome is just an earthly city while Jerusalem is divine, equating the Catholic Church with Jerusalem. Hence, the Roman Empire is no longer necessary because the Catholic Church now serves as the community of believers. As long as you believe in Jesus, you'll be saved. So Paul's ideas were systemized to create the Catholic Church.

Jesus said there's a divine spark within us, but it comes from Satan, not God. Therefore, we cannot trust this divine spark because we are inherently evil. Pride is seen as the start of every kind of sin, leading to the belief that following your heart leads to pride and thus to evil. Pride means you want to be better than God, which is inherently evil.

Pride is a longing for a preserved exultation, abandoning the basis on which the mind should be firmly fixed and becoming self-complacent. This happens when one is too pleased with themselves, deserting the changeless good in favor of oneself. This voluntary desertion leads to darkening and chilling of the will, making one susceptible to believing falsehoods and disobeying God's commandments.

Jesus taught us that we exist to be creative and seek truth for ourselves, but Paul teaches us that we must obey God because we cannot trust ourselves as we are easily led astray by the devil. The Catholic Church has teachings about original sin—being born evil—and Christ redeeming us. We should not think for ourselves or read the Bible, as it will lead to confusion and deviation from divine guidance.

Priests represent God on Earth, with the pope having supreme authority. Thus, if the pope tells you to take pride in being part of the church, you cannot do so because doing so would contradict the teachings that pride is inherently evil. The pope's word is seen as the ultimate truth—whatever he says is the word of God.

This leads to questions about whether believers should take pride in their identity within the Catholic Church and whether they can find satisfaction in its mission. The first teaching is original sin, with Christ redeeming us. The second is that we cannot think for ourselves or read the Bible independently; we must listen to priests and follow God's commandments strictly.

The Catholic Church's teachings lead to reformation, as the pope's authority is absolute, making any individual effort to pursue Jesus' teachings independent of church guidance inherently problematic.
